body.x: BLACKYAK I&C Co., Ltd. (CEO TAE HYO KIM) participated in the Global Media Online Meet-Up held on July 2 in collaboration with U.S. tech media outlet Ubergizmo, targeting Korean companies and startups.

The Global Media Meet-Up, co-hosted by AVING News and Ubergizmo, aims to introduce Korean products and technologies to the global market. It also aims to promote CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and exhibitors to international media ahead of the event, creating more business opportunities.

BLACKYAK I&C is a company that leads innovation in the safety sector, leveraging BLACKYAK’s technology and expertise in functional outdoor gear since 1973. Its main products include safety shoes, industrial safety equipment, and protective clothing. Recently, it has focused on developing smart PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) and systems for recycling waste from safety shoes, industrial safety gear, and clothing.

It is expanding its product line centered on the premium workwear brand ‘BLACKYAK WORKWEAR’ and the casual workwear brand ‘WORXONE’, enhancing its B2B and B2C distribution strategies. The company aims to lead the industrial safety workwear market within five years by investing in continuous technology development and product innovation with a focus on tech-driven safety gear.

BLACKYAK I&C strengthened its global brand presence by participating in the A+A Trade Fair for Occupational Safety and Health held in Düsseldorf, Germany, in 2023. The company achieved sales of 37.7 billion KRW last year, recording a 27% CAGR over the past four years, outpacing industry peers. In January 2025, it became the first company in Korea’s industrial safety market to be listed on KOSDAQ, proving its market value and credibility.

Now, it is aiming for a CES 2026 Innovation Award with ‘Sky Shield’, scheduled for release in the first half of 2026. High-altitude worksites often feature severe noise, dust, and expansive work areas, making it challenging to detect and respond quickly to fall accidents. Sky Shield is a smart wearable safety product designed to help managers detect such accidents within the critical time frame, thereby preventing secondary accidents.

body.cap: The smart wearable safety product ‘Sky Shield’ in action | Provided by BLACKYAK I&C

body.x: Sky Shield attaches to the shock absorber of the safety belt worn by high-altitude workers. When a fall occurs, the absorber tears, distributing the user’s weight, causing the attached red safety pin to disconnect. The device then automatically transmits GPS location data via Google Maps to emergency contacts through smartphone linkage. It also emits an ultrasonic signal from the device itself, allowing rescuers to cross-check the worker’s location for quicker rescue and prevention of secondary accidents.

The device features precision location transmission using audio and communication technologies. It sends exact coordinates to emergency contacts based on GPS data. It also boasts military-grade ruggedness (MIL-STD-810), maintaining consistent performance in extreme environments from -20°C to 60°C. With an ultra-low power architecture and energy-saving algorithm, it reduces maintenance costs and improves operational efficiency.

The product’s intuitive and stable modular design also stands out. Its simple carabiner-compatible interface allows anyone to use it easily, and its black-red color scheme enhances visual recognition as a safety device.

Made of durable aluminum, it withstands external forces in rough work environments and supports repeated use without malfunction. Its universal design allows compatibility with most harnesses supporting loads of 60-120kg, using a lower carabiner attachment method.

From an innovation standpoint, it shifts the paradigm from passive to active safety. Rather than merely preventing falls, it proactively reduces preventable damage, introducing a new active safety paradigm that does not leave accidents unattended.

It also incorporates cross-verification technology that combines GPS-based location transmission with 100dB ultrasonic beacon signals, enhancing location accuracy in environments such as tunnels, underground sites, and densely populated urban construction areas with weak GPS signals.

body.cap: The smart wearable safety product ‘Sky Shield’ | Provided by BLACKYAK I&C

body.x: BLACKYAK I&C emphasized Sky Shield’s ability to address global problems. Accidents in the workplace result in significant financial losses for companies and nations, including insurance payouts, treatment costs, human losses, project delays, and shutdowns. By preventing serious accidents, the product can help mitigate these losses.

It also offers a low-cost smart safety solution accessible to developing countries and SMEs that struggle to afford high-end safety systems, helping reduce blind spots and promoting industrial safety equality.
Sky Shield can also address the shortage of safety personnel. A single safety manager can monitor multiple high-altitude workers in real-time, helping maintain safety even at understaffed worksites.

The potential to build an IoT platform based on wearable devices will accelerate the digital transformation of industrial safety, laying the foundation for future integration with smart cities and smart factories.

BLACKYAK I&C plans to participate in CES for the first time in 2026. If it wins the Innovation Award, it expects to position itself as a smart and eco-friendly safety solution provider in the global industrial safety market.

Breaking from the traditional perception of industrial safety products as manufacturing-based, BLACKYAK I&C is pursuing a transition to a PPP (Personal Protective Platform). Winning at CES would be a catalyst for realizing this vision. As international regulations on industrial safety tighten, building trust as a global tech company would help diversify business opportunities, such as attracting VC investment, public R&D projects, and global B2B procurement deals.

body.cap: BLACKYAK I&C responds to media questions at the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Wednesday, July 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Looking ahead to CES 2027, BLACKYAK I&C plans to conduct direct sales activities targeting global buyers and partners, further executing its international expansion strategy.

It plans to focus first on countries with industrial safety markets structured similarly to Korea. Japan, with active tech exchanges with Korea and similar standards and regulations, has a low entry barrier. As construction workers age, physical accidents increase, and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport (MLIT) is promoting safety data systems as part of its construction DX policy. This is expanding the demand for smart safety devices like Sky Shield.

In Vietnam, where many Korean manufacturers, such as Samsung and LG, operate, trust in Korean products is high. Partnering with local safety distributors will facilitate the expansion of the B2B supply. Although PPE requirements are still in the early stages, demand for smart equipment is growing. BLACKYAK I&C views Vietnam as an environment where Sky Shield’s intuitive usability and reliability can spread quickly.

In the Middle East, where plant-based construction is prevalent and high-altitude work is common, demand for smart safety devices to prevent serious accidents is increasing. These markets actively import foreign technology and equipment, with foreign workers comprising a significant portion of the labor force. BLACKYAK I&C plans to highlight Sky Shield’s intuitive use and durability in this region.

body.cap: BLACKYAK I&C presents its pitch during the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Wednesday, July 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Ultimately, BLACKYAK I&C aims to demonstrate the effectiveness of its technology in the highly regulated industrial safety markets of the U.S. and Europe. In the U.S., demand for smart safety solutions that comply with strict OSHA standards is high due to the presence of high-altitude work in construction, utilities, communications, and industrial plants. In Europe, industries such as wind power, logistics, and facility maintenance are showing growing interest in AI-based fall detection and wearable PPE. CE certification enables wide distribution across the continent.

A BLACKYAK I&C official stated, “Sky Shield, set to launch in the first half of 2026, marks the beginning of BLACKYAK I&C’s smart industrial safety platform initiative. Starting with this product, we aim to build a Personal Protective Platform (PPP) that connects future smart wearable devices through an IoT system, evolving into an integrated platform capable of real-time risk detection, location tracking, and safety management based on user data.”

They added, “Our challenge for the CES 2026 Innovation Award is just the beginning. We plan to continue promoting our product and technology globally by participating in Japan’s Industrial Safety and Health Exhibition and Germany’s A+A Trade Fair for Occupational Safety and Health. Our goal is to simultaneously establish global leadership and market share in the smart safety device field.”

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo operates the Silicon Valley Post and publishes content in six languages across 200 countries, with a focus on electronics and technology. It regularly covers major global exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo co-founder and CTO Hubert Nguyen attended the event. He previously worked as an NVIDIA programming engineer, developer education program manager, and 3D graphics programmer. He covers products and technologies from around the world at CES each year.
